items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: I used to love the old man Jack Carey.

ctx.x: Who was your favorite of all the tromboners when you were young that you liked to listen to?

Well, I'll tell you, I used to love the old man Big Jasper. He was nice on trombone. Smooth, I played. But there was a further noise there. It was all the light, you see. So you'd get a kink out of them and see they could raise so much playing on that trombone. They'd give you a good time. You were a reading fellow, a good time. Yeah. Especially out in the street and everything I think I thought, but they had no stuff like you. I used to love the old man Jack Carey. He didn't know. Watch, I forgot.
I was going to ask about Jack Carey. How was he? He was a real good, uh-oh.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Jack was a good, you know, a good, he had a very good ear.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about the Jack Carey style so he could get an idea of what Jack Carey played like.

Jack was a good, you know, a good, he had a very good ear. He was speaking about that fast tone and all like that, Jack could do that and he was good, he could pop them notes high up there too and he was a good hummer, that means he called a singer on the trumpet. Well that was most of our style then, you know. The singer is the gliss or the slide? Yeah, like that. Now a tiger egg.
You said one time you did play quadrillo, huh?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: He was good. He was good. He was on that auditory. Jack was on that auditory.

ctx.x: Did he come up to that?
He was good. He was good. He was on that auditory. Jack was on that auditory. Mm-hmm. Pretty rough, huh?
